title: A Woman Among Women by Julia May Jonas at Lincoln Center Theatre #awo...
transcript: “Is this the worst acting I've ever seen?” is a thought that initially entered my mind until I quickly realised that no, every single one of these characters is just odd. In a riff on All My Sons by Arthur Miller through a matriarchal lens, A Woman Among Women by Julia May Jonas is a bizarre, nevertheless thought-provoking portrait of a community navigating the line between supporting and imposing. There's so much exposition with everyone catching up on each other's business that it's quite a while before any central conflict or plot materializes. The play is abundant with choices, distinctive but infrequently integrated into the story, making them come across as strange more than anything else. Why is there a reenactment of a family who died of consumption? Why are we the audience underscoring a scene change with a guided percussion session? Regardless, I was captivated by the main plot involving Cleo and her two adult daughters, one of whom is in prison for a crime made under troubling circumstances, the other feeling left in the shadows, never fully loved by her mother. While the crux of the piece does end up coming together and the exploration of morality and matriarchy is ripe with intrigue, it takes too long to get there. I thought there was a lot of filler, including entire characters that felt unnecessary to me. Sometimes, less is more and maybe this play could’ve more effectively accomplished everything it set out to do in 75 minutes instead of 100. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
